The paper reports both FDG-PET and VBM whole-brain, voxelwise results in MNI space and between-group contrasts (NC vs FTD) with sufficient sample sizes reported at least in aggregate; however the patient group is described only as ‘frontotemporal dementia (FTD)’ without specifying behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease. The study meets several inclusion criteria: it used VBM (I3), included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=58) (I4), has sufficient patient and control group sizes (I5), and reports whole-brain voxelwise results consistent with whole-brain evidence (I7) with acceptable reporting (I8). The study uses VBM (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4), has sufficient patient and control sample sizes (I5), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results from the target bvFTD sample (I7), and reports coordinates/peaks (I8). The study uses VBM (gray matter voxelwise morphometry) and includes a clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant FTD (bvFTD) group with sufficient sample size (bvFTD n≈18) and healthy controls (n≈18). The study uses VBM (voxel-based morphometry) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients with adequate sample sizes; however, the reported neuroimaging results are cross-subject voxelwise regressions of self–informant discrepancy across a mixed sample (patients and controls) rather than a between-group, whole-brain VBM contrast that compares the bvFTD group directly to healthy controls without pooling with other patient groups.
